look_here_first: Low prostrate creeping perennial with touch-sensitive leaves, pink globose heads, and broad prickly pods that do not narrow strongly between seeds.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; ITIS accepts species; UT PRC documents it as a native Hays County sensitive briar.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.
best_field_traits: pod body not strongly constricted between seeds
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The pod is the standout: broad and comparatively blocky rather than long and narrow. It is lower and more creeping than woody M. borealis or M. texana.
